chunks: That which the Sheikh — may God support him — reported to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him:
He said: I asked him about a man from whom wind passes — is he required to perform istinja'? He said: "No."

key_terms.أَيَّدَهُ اَللَّهُ: may God support him — a formula of blessing indicating the Sheikh was alive at time of writing
key_terms.اَلرِّيحُ: passing of wind, flatulence; nullifies wudu but does not obligate istinja'
key_terms.اَلشَّيْخُ: the Sheikh (here: Sheikh al-Mufid, teacher of al-Tusi, through whom this chain reaches the author)
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِيَ: to perform istinja': the ritual cleansing of the private parts after excretion

ai.seo_question: Does passing wind require istinja' according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith records a direct question posed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) by his companion 'Ammar al-Sabati: does the passage of wind (flatulence) require a person to perform istinja' (ritual cleansing of the private parts)? The Imam's unambiguous single-word answer — 'No' — establishes that istinja' is specific to the exits of urine and feces, and that wind, though a nullifier of wudu, does not trigger the obligation of istinja'.
